COP ticked up 0.37% today to $137.04, extending a four-day climb that's added nearly 3% since last Tuesday. The move reflects the pull-and-tug in crude markets: while oil prices fell sharply today after weeks above $100 a barrel, the underlying tightness in global energy supply—diesel hitting record highs, refineries running at capacity, and Houthi advances threatening shipping through the Bab el-Mandeb Strait—keeps the longer-term backdrop supportive for an integrated oil and gas company like this one. ConocoPhillips benefits when crude stays elevated and refining margins stay fat, which the strained global refining system suggests they will for now.

The gap between U.S. crude ($97.26/barrel) and world crude ($109.51/barrel) is unusually wide—a sign that global supply chains are genuinely constrained and that U.S. producers with access to export markets or downstream refining stand to gain. That structural tightness, driven by the Iran and Ukraine conflicts, has cushioned the stock even as prices pulled back today.
